key_insight: CPAPIR was refurbished by replacing a degraded detector and converting its cooling from liquid nitrogen to a cryocooler-based system to extend instrument life and improve operability.
engineering_relevance: The upgrade shows how thermal-mechanical redesign, FEA, and hardware integration can modernize aging scientific instruments while reducing maintenance burden.
method: 3D CAD redesign of the detector and cryocooler integration
Finite element analysis to assess thermal and mechanical performance
Laboratory validation with attention to vibration mitigation and cryogenic implementation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful design, integration, and lab testing of the upgraded system, with on-sky commissioning planned for summer 2026.
watch_item: Cryocooler integration can introduce vibration and alignment challenges that must be managed carefully during commissioning.
paper_title: Refurbishment and Cryocooler Upgrade of the CPAPIR Wide-Field Near-Infrared Camera: Design, Integration, and Lessons Learned
